title: Energy & Water — Reducing Our Impact
blurb: Simple daily habits that cut the energy and water we waste and bring our running costs down.
siteNotes: Your manager will show you the end-of-service switch-off routine for your area.
Who to tell about leaks, broken seals or heating and lighting left on in empty areas.
legalNotes: Nothing in this trainer rests on a legal rule; it is good practice for cost and the environment. No figures are stated.

cards.title: Energy & Water — Reducing Our Impact
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- say why saving energy and water matters
- switch off, close up and use water sensibly
- report leaks and faults promptly

cards.title: Small habits, big difference
cards.body:
Being greener cuts our running costs as well as helping the planet. Energy and water are two of the easiest places to make an impact, and it mostly comes down to not wasting what we do not need.

Lots of small habits from everyone add up.

cards.title: Use what you need, switch off the rest
cards.body:
Switch off lights, equipment and appliances when they are not in use, rather than leaving them on or on standby. Turn things off properly at the end of service.

Close external doors and windows when the heating or air-con is running.

left.title: Do
items: Switch off lights when not needed
Switch equipment off, not to standby
Close doors with heating or air-con on
Turn things off at end of service

right.title: Do not
items: Leave lights on in empty areas

cards.title: Kettles and fridges
cards.body:
Do not overfill the kettle. Make sure fridges and freezers seal properly and are not left open.

A fridge door left open or a worn seal wastes energy all day.

cards.title: Do not let it run
cards.body:
Do not leave taps running. A dripping tap wastes a surprising amount, so report it promptly.

Only run dishwashers and washing machines with full loads, and use the right amount rather than the most. In the kitchen and cellar, mop up and manage water sensibly.

cards.title: Report what you notice
cards.body:
Report faults like leaks, broken seals, or heating and lighting left on in empty areas.

None of this is complicated. It is just being switched-on, and switching things off.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Switch off lights and equipment when not in use; standby still uses energy.
- Close external doors and windows when heating or air-con is running.
- Report drips, leaks, broken seals and heating or lighting left on in empty areas.
- Run dishwashers and washing machines with full loads.
- Small habits from everyone add up to a big difference.

cards.q: Saving energy and water cuts our running costs as well as helping the environment.
cards.why: Being greener cuts our running costs too, as well as helping the environment.

cards.q: When the heating or air-con is on, external doors should be…
cards.why: Close external doors and windows when the heating or air-con is running.

cards.q: What should you do with lights and equipment when they are not in use?
options: Leave them on standby for next time
Leave them on until end of service
Dim them and leave them running
cards.why: Switch off lights, equipment and appliances when they are not in use, rather than leaving them on or on standby.

cards.q: A dripping tap wastes a surprising amount of water and should be reported.
cards.why: A dripping tap wastes a surprising amount, so report it promptly.

cards.q: Dishwashers and washing machines should be run…
options: On a short cycle every time
cards.why: Only run dishwashers and washing machines with full loads.

cards.q: Leaving equipment on standby uses no energy.
cards.why: Standby still uses energy. Switch equipment off rather than leaving it on standby.

cards.q: Which of these should you report to help save energy or water?
options: A tap that is turned off
A fridge door that is shut
A kettle filled for one cup
cards.why: Report faults like leaks, broken seals, or heating and lighting left on in empty areas.
Do not overfill the kettle; heating water you do not need wastes energy.

options: Add up to a big difference
Cost the venue more in time
cards.why: Lots of small habits from everyone add up to a big difference.

cards.q: Fridge and freezer doors left open waste energy.
cards.why: Fridges and freezers should seal properly and not be left open.
